This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.781/2022 dated 31.12.2022, registered at P.S.-
Rahatgarh, District- Sagar (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 376(3), 376(2)(n), 376-D,
376(2)(f), 506/34 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.

A s per the prosecution story, on 30.12.2022 19 year old prosecutrix moved an application before Smt. Babli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188109990/
1 Mahila Thana Sagar alleging that her parents have died 15 years ago.

entities.text: Smt. Babli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After the death of parents, she along with her younger sister started to reside with her elder sister in her in laws house at Khari Gumariya.
When she was about 13 years old she was raped by her brother-in-law Lakhan and his younger brother Raju.
When she told that she will make the complaint, they used to threaten her to drove out of the home and also eliminate her.
On account of continuous rape by both brothers, she became pregnant.
In the year 2021, she was taken to a Hospital in Gujarat and there she had delivered a girl child who is with them.
In May 2022, she entered into wedlock with Rahul.
Thereafter she narrated the entire story to her husband and due to courage instilled in her by husband she lodged FIR.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicants have not committed any offence.
They are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated.
The only allegation against them is that of screening the evidence and the factum of delivery of girl child by the prosecutrix on account of repeated rape by Lakhan and his younger brother Raju.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Applicants have no knowledge about the rape with the prosecutrix by Lakhan and Raju.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicants/accused be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and the allegation against the applicants who are the women, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pretrial detention of both the applicants/accused is not warranted.
Consequently, first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicants, stands allowed.

It is directed that applicants-Babli and Jyoti be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
They shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE b Smt. Babli vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188109990/
